statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the collection of all k-element subsets of {1,2,...,n}, represented as lists with arbitrary outer order and arbitrary order inside each list: (1) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), len(r[i]) = k, the entries of r[i] are pairwise distinct, and every entry lies in {1,2,...,n}; (2) for every subset S of {1,2,...,n} with |S| = k, there is exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that the set of entries of r[i] is S.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: For every n and k satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail due to overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = C(n,k), where C(n,k) = n!/(k!(n-k)!) is the number of k-element subsets of {1,2,...,n}.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), len(r[i]) = k.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r) and every j with 0 <= j < len(r[i]), 1 <= r[i][j] <= n, interpreting each r[i][j] as a mathematical integer.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r) and all j1, j2 with 0 <= j1 < j2 < len(r[i]), r[i][j1] != r[i][j2].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every subset S of {1,2,...,n} with |S| = k, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that the set of entries of r[i] is exactly S.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for all i1 and i2 with 0 <= i1 < i2 < len(r), the set of entries of r[i1] is not equal to the set of entries of r[i2].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every v with 1 <= v <= n, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that v occurs among the entries of r[i] equals C(n-1,k-1), where C(a,b) is the binomial coefficient a!/(b!(a-b)!).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair (a,b) with 1 <= a < b <= n, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that both a and b occur among the entries of r[i] equals C(n-2,k-2) if k >= 2, and equals 0 if k = 1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the sum of all entries of all inner lists, namely sum over 0 <= i < len(r) and 0 <= j < len(r[i]) of r[i][j], equals C(n-1,k-1) * n(n+1)/2, interpreting the sum and the product as mathematical integers.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and k = n, len(r) = 1 and the unique inner list r[0] is a permutation of [1,2,...,n], i.e. its entries are exactly 1,2,...,n in some order.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and k = 1, len(r) = n and for every v with 1 <= v <= n there is exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that r[i] is the singleton list [v].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 20 and 1 <= k <= n, where n and k denote the mathematical integer values of the Std.I64 arguments.
